The Locust God has incredible synergy with Zndrsplt already on board - each coin flip win draws a card, and each draw creates a 1/1 flying haste Insect. Lightning Greaves was also available to protect it.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed the main phase without casting any spells or playing a land
annotations.betterLine: Play Rogue's Passage as land drop, cast The Locust God for 4UR, and potentially cast Lightning Greaves to protect it. This sets up a powerful card advantage + token generation engine with Zndrsplt.

annotations.description: Gem3F Analyst had The Locust God available to cast with sufficient mana (7 untapped sources for a 4UR spell) before Zndrsplt's coin-flip trigger resolved. The Locust God creates a 1/1 flying haste Insect for each card drawn, so casting it before the trigger would generate bonus Insect tokens from every coin flip win. Missing this sequencing wastes significant value from the Zndrsplt synergy.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to cast anything before Zndrsplt's trigger resolved.
annotations.betterLine: Cast The Locust God (4UR) before Zndrsplt's trigger resolves, so each card drawn from won coin flips creates a 1/1 flying haste Insect token.

annotations.description: Declined to activate The Locust God's loot ability ({2}{U}{R}: Draw a card, then discard a card) during combat with plenty of untapped mana available. This would have provided card filtering and created a 1/1 flying haste Insect token for free, which is pure upside.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed on all options during combat, dealing only 7 damage with existing attackers.
annotations.betterLine: Activate The Locust God's ability to loot, gaining card selection and a free 1/1 Insect creature token. With Island, Mountain, Command Tower, Temple of Epiphany, Exotic Orchard, and Arcane Signet all untapped, there was more than enough mana.

annotations.description: Gem3F Analyst had access to The Locust God (castable at 6 mana with 7 untapped sources) and an unplayed land drop (Rogue's Passage) during postcombat main. The Locust God is an extremely powerful threat that generates flying tokens on each draw. Missing either the land drop or failing to deploy this threat represents a significant missed opportunity.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed the turn or made a less impactful play instead of deploying The Locust God and playing Rogue's Passage
annotations.betterLine: Play Rogue's Passage for the land drop, then cast The Locust God using available mana (Island, Mountain, Arcane Signet, Command Tower, Temple of Epiphany, Exotic Orchard provides {4}{U}{R})

annotations.description: Sevinne, the Chronoclasm prevents all damage dealt to it, making it a risk-free attacker. Not attacking with Sevinne leaves free damage on the table every turn. While Dockside Extortionist's ETB has already triggered making it less valuable to keep alive, Sevinne should always be attacking since it's indestructible in combat.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Dockside Extortionist (1/2), leaving Sevinne (2/2, indestructible) back on defense
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Sevinne and Dockside Extortionist, or at minimum attack with Sevinne since it cannot die in combat and represents free damage every turn

annotations.description: Sevinne, the Chronoclasm prevents all damage dealt to it, making it a risk-free attacker every turn. Not attacking with Sevinne leaves 2 guaranteed damage on the table while instead attacking with the vulnerable 1/2 Dockside Extortionist.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Dockside Extortionist (1/2), leaving Sevinne (2/2, damage-immune) back on defense.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Sevinne and Dockside Extortionist, or at minimum attack with Sevinne since it cannot be damaged and is always a free attacker.

annotations.description: Attacking Sonnet Rules with a 1/2 Dockside Extortionist into a board with Shimmer Myr (2/2) and Aeronaut Admiral (3/1) is questionable. Sonnet Rules can easily block and kill the Extortionist. If unblocked, 1 damage to a 34-life player is nearly meaningless. Attacking Gem3F Analyst (32 life) would be equally low-impact but at least Gem3F has fewer potential blockers on the ground (Zndrsplt is tapped). However, the bigger question is whether attacking at all is worth risking the Dockside Extortionist, which could be relevant later as a body or for sacrifice synergies. Sonnet Rules has two creatures that can block and trade favorably.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked Sonnet Rules with Dockside Extortionist (1/2)
annotations.betterLine: Either attack Gem3F Analyst where blockers are tapped/less threatening, or don't attack at all to preserve Dockside Extortionist as a blocker/resource.

annotations.description: Chose Shimmer Myr (2/2) for Kotori's lifelink+vigilance trigger instead of Foundry Inspector (3/2), which has higher power and would gain more life from lifelink when attacking.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Shimmer Myr with Kotori's combat trigger for lifelink and vigilance
annotations.betterLine: Target Foundry Inspector (3/2) with Kotori's trigger to maximize lifelink damage (3 life vs 2 life per attack)

annotations.description: Attacking Gem3F Analyst at 32 life for 5 damage is less impactful than attacking GPT5m Minimal at 20 life. 5 damage into 32 life barely matters, while 5 into 20 puts real pressure on and moves toward elimination.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked Gem3F Analyst (32 life) for 5 damage
annotations.betterLine: Attack GPT5m Minimal (20 life) for 5, bringing them to 15 and into a much more vulnerable range for elimination

annotations.description: Gem3F Analyst cast Krark's Thumb before playing Rogue's Passage as their land for the turn. Playing lands before casting spells is fundamental sequencing - it maximizes available mana and information. Additionally, Lightning Greaves might have been a stronger play to protect the key engine piece Zndrsplt from removal, especially with Sonnet having Shimmer Myr allowing flash-speed interaction.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Krark's Thumb without first making land drop (Rogue's Passage was available)
annotations.betterLine: Play Rogue's Passage first, then cast Krark's Thumb (or consider Lightning Greaves to protect Zndrsplt)

annotations.description: Gem3F Analyst had exactly 2 mana available (Command Tower + Arcane Signet) and could have cast Lightning Greaves to protect Zndrsplt, Eye of Wisdom with shroud. Zndrsplt is a key card draw engine and protecting it is valuable. Instead, they passed without casting anything.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without casting any spells despite having Lightning Greaves available at exactly 2 mana.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Lightning Greaves for 2 mana and equip it to Zndrsplt, Eye of Wisdom to grant it shroud and protect the card draw engine.

annotations.description: Cast Krark before playing a land drop. They had Sulfur Falls (which enters untapped since they control an Island) in hand and should have played it first to maximize available mana for the rest of the turn, potentially holding up Long-Term Plans (2U) or other responses.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Krark, the Thumbless without first making a land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Sulfur Falls first (enters untapped), then cast Krark, the Thumbless, leaving more mana open for Long-Term Plans or other instant-speed plays

annotations.description: Played Inventors' Fair which only produces colorless mana and has no active abilities (only 1 artifact controlled, needs 3). Sulfur Falls would enter untapped and produce colored mana (U or R), which is more useful for casting spells like Long-Term Plans or Blasphemous Act.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Inventors' Fair as the land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Sulfur Falls (enters untapped since an Island is controlled), providing flexible colored mana. Inventors' Fair could be saved for a later turn when more artifacts are in play to activate its abilities.

annotations.description: Gem3F Analyst passed their entire precombat main phase without playing a land, despite having Sulfur Falls, Buried Ruin, and Desolate Lighthouse in hand. Missing a land drop in a 1v1 situation where mana development matters is a clear mistake. Additionally, they could have considered casting Blasphemous Act to remove Sonnet Rules' Aeronaut Admiral and Shimmer Myr, though losing Zndrsplt makes that more debatable.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed the precombat main phase without taking any action, including not playing a land.
annotations.betterLine: At minimum, play a land (Desolate Lighthouse or Sulfur Falls for color fixing and utility). Could also consider Blasphemous Act to clear the opponent's board, or Long-Term Plans to set up a key card.

annotations.description: Kotori's trigger grants lifelink AND vigilance. Silver Myr benefits more from vigilance because it has a tap ability ({T}: Add {U}), meaning it could attack for 1 life and still produce mana. The Myr Token has no tap ability, so vigilance is wasted on it compared to Silver Myr.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Myr Token with Kotori's lifelink and vigilance trigger
annotations.betterLine: Target Silver Myr with Kotori's trigger, allowing it to attack for 1 (gaining 1 life from lifelink) while still being able to tap for blue mana thanks to vigilance

annotations.description: Gem3F Analyst has The Locust God available to cast with sufficient mana (6 sources for 4UR), which creates a devastating engine with Zndrsplt already on board - every coin flip win draws a card AND creates a 1/1 flying haste Insect. Instead they cast a 2-mana rock that provides minimal value at this stage of the game.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Thought Vessel for incremental mana advantage and no maximum hand size
annotations.betterLine: Cast The Locust God to establish a game-winning synergy with Zndrsplt, Eye of Wisdom. Each combat's coin flips would generate cards and flying attackers, quickly closing out the game against Sonnet Rules at 16 life.

annotations.description: Gem3F Analyst passed without casting anything despite having cheap, useful plays available. Lightning Greaves (2 mana) could protect Zndrsplt, Eye of Wisdom with shroud, which is their key card draw engine in a 1v1 against Sonnet Rules at 16hp. Shadowspear (1 mana) could also be deployed cheaply for later use.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting any spells during precombat main phase.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Lightning Greaves for 2 mana and equip it to Zndrsplt for free to grant shroud, protecting the key card advantage engine. Could also consider casting Shadowspear for 1 mana.

annotations.description: Gem3F Analyst declined to cast Embercleave during combat, dealing only 5 damage instead of 11. With 2 attacking creatures, Embercleave costs {2}{R}{R}, and they had exactly the mana (Island, Arcane Signet, Spinerock Knoll, Command Tower, Temple of Epiphany - 5 mana with 3+ red available). Attaching Embercleave to The Locust God would make it a 5/5 with double strike and trample, dealing 10+1=11 damage, putting Sonnet Rules to 5 life instead of 11. In a 1v1 endgame situation, this 6 extra damage is very significant.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to cast Embercleave, attacking for only 5 damage total (1+4)
annotations.betterLine: Cast Embercleave during combat (costs {2}{R}{R} with 2 attackers), attach to The Locust God for 11 total damage, putting Sonnet Rules to 5 life and threatening lethal next turn
